rejected.title: Australia's distinctive landscapes
card: Australia is mostly flat and dry, with very long coasts. Much of the centre is desert, with little rain.
The Great Dividing Range runs down the east. It is a long line of highlands, and it is the main mountain system in the east.
Parts of the north, where it is hot and wet, have tropical rainforest. These are patches only: much of the north is grassy woodland.
Some landforms are famous, such as Uluru, a huge rock in the desert of central Australia.
rejected.remember: Australia is mostly flat and dry, with highlands in the east and patches of rainforest in the north.

a.q: Which description best fits most of Australia's landscape?
a.why: Most of Australia is flat and dry, with deserts in the centre. Rainforests are found in parts of the north, but they cover only a small part of the country.
a.clue: Think of the centre of the country.

b.q: Priya flies over Australia looking for tropical rainforest. Where could she find it?
opts: In hot, wet patches of the north
Across almost all of the north
Across most of the dry centre
b.why: Tropical rainforest grows in hot, wet parts of the north, but only in patches. Much of the north is grassy woodland, so saying it covers almost all of the north is wrong.
b.clue: Is the rainforest spread right across the north, or only in parts?

flags: Question b, other: The clue ('Is the rainforest spread right across the north, or only in parts?') rules out the main distractor and points straight to the 'patches' option, so students can answer without knowing the idea.

draft.title: Australia's distinctive landscapes
card: Australia is mostly flat and dry. Much of the centre is desert, with little rain.
The Great Dividing Range runs down the east. It is a long line of highlands, and it is the main mountain system in the east.

draft.remember: Australia is mostly flat and dry, with highlands in the east and wetter lands in the north.

a.q: Which description best fits most of Australia's landscape?
a.why: Most of Australia is flat and dry, with deserts in the centre. Rainforests are found in the north, but they cover only a small part of the country.
a.clue: Think of the centre of the country.

b.q: Priya travels from the central desert to the far north of Australia. Which change in landscape would she most likely see?
opts: Dry desert gives way to tropical rainforest
Dry desert gives way to snowy highlands
Tropical rainforest gives way to flat grassland
Flat desert gives way to the Great Dividing Range
b.why: The north is hot and wet, so tropical rainforests grow there. The Great Dividing Range is in the east, not the north, so it is not the change she would see.
b.clue: The north is hot and wet.

b.best: Dry desert gives way to tropical rainforest

problems.detail: Most of northern Australia is tropical savanna (grassy woodland), and rainforest grows only in patches such as the Wet Tropics, Cape York and parts of the Top End. Asking what Priya would 'most likely' see suggests the far north is mainly rainforest. The card's 'The north has tropical rainforests' supports that reading without saying the rainforests are patchy. A wording such as 'could see' or 'parts of the north have tropical rainforests' would be safer.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer and the card is accurate overall. The card and question b suggest the far north is mainly rainforest, when most of it is tropical savanna and rainforest occurs in patches.
